hook: The Presidio & Ferries Railroad's horse car barn, remodelled and still standing in the Jackson Square Historic District.
survey_name: Presidio and Ferries Railroad car barn
survey_name_note: SF Planning records the name as "PRESIDIO AND FERRIES RAILROAD CAR BAR", truncated by the field width.

parcel.note: Business addresses are usually deferred on this site; this page exists because the address was named in the prompting source. The parcel spans 440 and 444 Jackson Street, and DBI files the same permits under both numbers.

historic_status.ceqa_status_label: Historical resource; within an Article 10 historic district
historic_status.reason: Article 10 Historic District, National Register Historic District, California Register Historic District, Historic Survey Result

historic_district.name: Jackson Square Historic District
historic_district.note: The district returns two rows over the same ground; the Article 10 designation and the National/California Register listings are merged here.

permits.description: entry modified inside and out under the accessible business entrance program
tenant improvement of the retail space — partitions, a door, fixtures, finishes, electrical, mechanical and plumbing
non-structural demolition of partitions, lighting and millwork
barrier removal — bathroom renovated to be accessible, a wall moved and fixtures replaced
seismic retrofit under a city loan, with a new landing

permits_note: Six of the 22 filings on this parcel are shown; the rest are sign and street-space permits, cancelled applications, and the duplicates DBI files under both 440 and 444 Jackson Street.

historical_record.description: The Presidio & Ferries Railroad ran a horse car section along Washington and Jackson Streets, connecting the ferry terminals to its cable railway terminal. Its horse cars were stabled in the car barn here.
Cable service on the Presidio & Ferries ended when the earthquake and fire destroyed the railroad's infrastructure.
